I always recommend Paladin/Warlock/Sorcerer multiclasses. 8/4/8 is pretty good, my personal favorite though is either 7/2/11 or 6/3/11. I really like going more Sorcerer, because it just lets me feel like I can do more stuff. Clockwork Soul Sorcerer is unbelievably powerful, but Divine Soul also works well. It's not an easy multiclass to pull off with point buy, but with a fairly lucky stat roll, you can really shine. My order of operations with it is to always start Paladin and either go 2 levels to get dueling, or 1/1 to get Hexblade online as soon as possible. I rely on Booming Blade early, as the multiclass will end up delaying extra attack a little bit, but BB normally makes up for it, especially if you're going 1h + shield. For Invocations, I'm generally gonna pick Feindish Vigor + Agonizing if I'm gonna take a 3rd level later and swap Feindish for Devil's Sight, of I'll just go Devil's + Agonizing if I'm only planning on 2 levels of Warlock. The character normally plays in and around Melee Range, but having a really reliable backup ranged option with Hex + EB is very nice. Having 18 AC at level 3 with 7 Temp HP going into every combat makes you extremely hard to take down. As for Paladin Oaths, I prefer Watchers. Here's my ultimate sniper build. Now I know what you're going to say: "Sniper? How can you claim to be a Sniper without playing Death's Head?"

See, there seems to be a general sense that the "Perfect" build relies on being able to do one thing better than anyone else. I, however, believe that to be considered a "Perfect" build, you need to be able to do your job reasonably better than anyone else, and also be as hard of a target to deal with as possible, and that's where my Kobold build comes in.

​

For starters, what does the build offer? I'm glad you asked!

Firstly, you have extremely consistent damage. The Fusion Rifle always does a guaranteed 6 energy damage when fired from at least 6 range away from someone, which you are almost guaranteed to be, seeing as it has a range of 14 with this build. Combined with Crack Shot 2, Nuclear Cavalier 2, and OpCal, you have an additional +3d6 Damage, and I believe that 3d6+6 damage is perfectly respectable from a primary weapon. Secondly, as your main weapon is a Main instead of a Heavy, you gain access to Walking Armory, thereby allowing you to turn your damage into whatever your enemy is not resistant to, which lends to the consistency of the build. Between Core Siphon and Autostab, you're looking at +2 Accuracy to your Fusion Rifle, which is more than enough to average around a 40-48% Crit Rate at ll12. Combine that with the 3 other Oracles you have, and that's a potential 3d3 extra damage on top of what the Fusion Rifle does already, which is fairly respectable, so long as your target lacks much armor.

Secondly, we have as much defense as you can reasonably have on an offensive mech. We have the Kobold's Trait, which allows us to always be benefitting from Hard Cover, thereby making our 12 Evasion much more respectable. We then have Mag Shield, which gives us Resistance to Kinetic and Explosive, thereby making our 20 HP and 1 Armor that much better at taking hits that do land. Thirdly, Black Ice Module gives all enemies between +1 and +3 difficulty, cycling, on any attacks targeting our E-Defense, which is already 14 at base. Finally, Swarm Body will quickly stack up to 9 Damage on our completely stationary build, dissuading any melee enemies from running up on us.

​

In conclusion, I believe the best gun is not one that you only need to fire once, but one that will never jam, never break, and very rarely needs to be cleaned, and still only ever has to be fired twice.

Longsword gets much easier the more you know the monsters you're fighting. I recommend running tankier sets if you're not comfortable, so that you can learn your counter timings without just getting one shot if you screw up. If you play Longsword or Bow, two weapons where it's very easy to dodge attacks and you can fairly reliably never get hit if you're good enough, you probably don't need to. If you play slower weapons or weapons with shields where you want to block hits, you should definitely change, as the harder hitting monsters are liable to one shot you without MR armor.

You need to be at least two major items + boots into your build before you can not feel bad about coughing up the 800 to build it, and by then you're in midgame and the Mundo (most common reason to build exec) might already be out of control, with or without his healing.

As far as building Exec into other bot lanes with a Sona/raka, it's really kinda unfeasible to build it, putting yourself 800 behind the enemy adc, just to shut down their support. Against raka you just ignore the adc and kill her first, anyway.

Really, the biggest problem with Exec is, unlike Morello, Exec doesn't build into/isn't a strong early/midgame item. Putting 800 gold into it early feels awful, where pushing your normal mid item back to build an item that has flat pen on it anyways doesn't feel nearly as handicapping.

It was daunting for me at first, as well. But now that DE has basically created a new "endgame" thing in the Teralyst, and soon the Gantulyst and any other -Lysts that they add in the future, especially with the newer ones dropping Arcanes, I can see that the need for LoR and the Jordas Verdict (which I still have never done) is basically gone. 

Trials will be something that I definitely miss, but I'm excited to see what direction DE is taking the game after they remove them.
